Never opened Logic?

Start Here

If you have never used Logic Pro, do these ten steps in order. By the end you will have played a sound, recorded it, and saved a file you can send to someone. Underlined words are explained in the Glossary at the back of the book.

Every trick marked START HERE in the book is safe for day one.

  1. 1

    Learn the four parts of the screen

    The control bar runs across the top: play, record, volume, and the display showing where you are in the song and its tempo. The big middle area is the Tracks area, where you record and arrange. The Library sits on the left and holds sounds. The Inspector shows settings for whatever you have selected.

    Source Apple — Main window interface (10.7 guide) · Apple — Inspector interface

  2. 2

    Know what a track and a region are

    A track is one lane in the Tracks area: one instrument or one microphone. A region is a block of recorded audio or MIDI sitting on a track. You move, copy and cut regions to build a song.

    Source Apple — Main window interface (10.7 guide) · Apple — Create tracks

  3. 3

    Add a track

    Click the Add Tracks button (the + above the track headers). In the New Tracks dialog pick Software Instrument to play sounds from a keyboard, Audio to record a microphone or guitar, or Drummer for a virtual drummer that plays a region for you.

    Source Apple — Create tracks · Apple — Drummer overview (10.7 guide)

  4. 4

    Pick a sound in the Library

    Select the track, open the Library, choose a category on the left and a patch on the right. The track now plays that sound.

    Y

    Source Apple — Choose a patch

  5. 5

    Play it without a keyboard

    No MIDI keyboard? Turn on Musical Typing and play notes on your computer keys. Z and X move down and up an octave. A software instrument track must be selected.

    ⌘K

    Source Apple — Play software instruments

  6. 6

    Play, stop, and go back to the start

    Space starts and stops playback. Return jumps the playhead back to the beginning of the project.

    Space

    Source Apple — Transport key commands (10.7 guide) · Apple — Control playback (10.7 guide)

  7. 7

    Record

    Select the track, press R, play, then press Space to stop. A new region appears on the track with what you played.

    R

    Source Apple — Record to multiple audio tracks

  8. 8

    Undo anything

    Made a mistake? Undo steps back one edit at a time; Redo puts it back. Experiment freely.

    ⌘Z

    Source Apple — Undo and redo edits

  9. 9

    Save often

    Save writes the project to disk. Logic also keeps backups of earlier saves you can revert to from the File menu.

    ⌘S

    Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups

  10. 10

    Export a file you can share

    Bounce turns your project into an audio file, such as a WAV or MP3, that plays anywhere.

    ⌘B

    Source Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file

Find it by what you want to make

I Want To…

You do not need to know what a feature is called. Find what you are trying to do below and go straight to the tricks that do it. Numbers are trick numbers; tricks tagged START HERE come first in each list.

Start here

How to Use This Book

Do not read this front to back. Jump to the section that matches what you are stuck on right now, take the trick, and get back to the music. Every section is one click away from every page.

Each entry is short on purpose. Title, what it does, the key command. Ten seconds to read, yours for good.

  • Every key command shown is the Logic Pro factory default on a US keyboard. If you have remapped anything, open Key Commands with ⌥K and search the command name — the name is always given.
  • Where a trick lives in a menu rather than on a key, the full menu path is written out, so it stays correct across versions.
  • This edition covers Logic Pro 11 and 12. Earlier versions differ in ways that would make some of these wrong — 10.7 calls Settings “Preferences” and the View pane “Display”, among others — so it is not written for them.
  • Every trick shows the source it was checked against — usually Apple's own Logic Pro guide — and the link is live, so you can read the original. Anything that could not be confirmed against a source was cut rather than printed on a guess. Tricks with no source are workflow habits, not claims about what Logic does.
  • Tricks marked GAME CHANGER are the ones worth stealing first.
  • Nothing here requires third-party plugins. It is all stock Logic.

The one habit that matters most

Every time you catch yourself doing something with the mouse for the third time, check whether it has a key command. If it does, learn it. If it does not, make one. That single habit is worth more than any individual trick in this book.

Key Legend

Logic's documentation and this book both use the Mac modifier symbols. If you are coming from another DAW, this is the page to bookmark.

⌥Option
⌥ (Option): Option-drag copies a region; Option-click a Solo button for an exclusive solo.1,2
⇧Shift
Shift-click to add to a selection.3,4
⌃Control
⌃ (Control): Control-click a selected region to open its shortcut menu.5
↩Return
↩ (Return): Sends the playhead to the start of the project.6,7
⌫Delete
⌫ (Delete): Deletes the selected regions.8
␣Space
␣ (Space): Play / Stop.9,10

Three modifier rules that explain most of Logic

Hold ⌥ while dragging a region and you copy it instead of moving it. ⌥-click a channel's Volume fader and it returns to 0 dB. ⌥-click a Solo button and it becomes an exclusive solo — that channel alone.

Source Apple — Cut, copy, and paste regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Set channel strip volume in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Mute and solo channel strips in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 01 · 29 tricks

Setting Up Logic.

Before a single note goes down, get the program out of your way. These are the settings worth checking on a fresh install, and each one says exactly where it lives.

Audio settings

No. 001GAME CHANGER

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Run two buffer sizes, not one

Open Settings with ⌘, and go to Audio > Devices. Keep the I/O Buffer Size small while you track so monitoring latency stays low. Raise it when you mix: a larger buffer lowers the load on your Mac's CPU. A buffer too small for your Mac shows up as clicks, pops and crackles.

⌘,

Source Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Overview of Logic Pro settings

No. 002

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Set Processing Threads to Automatic

In Settings > Audio > Devices, Processing Threads is set to Automatic by default, and Apple recommends leaving it there. The one exception Apple names: set a thread count yourself when you run other CPU-intensive apps at the same time as Logic.

Source Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 003

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Choose the right Multithreading mode

In Settings > Audio > Devices, the Multithreading pop-up offers two modes. Playback Tracks is the older behaviour: when several audio tracks record, or a Track Stack is selected for live input, all the input DSP runs on one thread and one core. Playback & Live Tracks spreads that load across threads but adds slightly more overall load. Use it only if you have demanding live tracks.

Source Apple — About the Multithreading setting in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

No. 004

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Set Process Buffer Range to Large to avoid overloads

In Settings > Audio > Devices, Process Buffer Range sets the buffer Logic uses to compute mixes and effects. It is separate from the I/O buffer and offers Small, Medium and Large. Apple's advice for avoiding system overloads is to set it to Large.

Source Apple — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

No. 005

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Uncheck Software Monitoring if you monitor through your interface

If your audio interface supports hardware (direct) monitoring, turn off Software Monitoring in Settings > Audio > General. With it on, your input is processed in software and some latency is unavoidable. Apple's advice is to switch it off whenever you listen through your interface or mixing console.

Source Apple — General Audio settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — General Audio settings in Logic Pro for Mac (IS locale)

Recording

No. 006Start here

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Leave Allow Quick Punch-In on

Apple's guide says Allow Quick Punch-In is on by default and recommends leaving it on: it lets you punch in and out of recording on the fly while the project keeps playing. Check it under Record > Allow Quick Punch-In, or Control-click the Record button in the control bar. Turn it off only if you record more tracks than there are channel strips (more than 128 in a new project) or your disk can't keep up.

Source Why Logic Pro Rules — Never Lose An Audio Take Again With Quick Punch-In · Why Logic Pro Rules — #16 Autopunch, Quick Punch-In, & Replace Recording Modes · Apple — Punch in and out of audio recordings in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 007

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Make the bar and the beat click sound different

In the project settings, the Metronome pane controls the audio click, which comes from Klopfgeist, a virtual metronome sound source on the Click channel strip. Separate Note and Velocity fields set the note number and velocity of the notes generated for the bar, group, beat or division, so you can make the bar and the beat sound different. The Tone slider changes the sound from a short click to a pitched percussion sound like a wood block or claves. The Audio Click checkbox also works with any other plug-in you load on the Click channel strip.

Source Apple — Metronome project settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Klopfgeist in Logic Pro for Mac

MIDI

No. 008

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Turn on scrubbing with audio in the Tracks area

Settings > Audio > Editing > “Scrubbing with audio in Tracks area”. With it on, you can scrub audio regions in the Tracks area with the Scissors or Solo tool and find a spot by ear. Maximum Scrub Speed and Scrub Response fine-tune how it feels.

Source Apple — Audio Editing settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 009

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Leave the MIDI Reset Messages at their defaults

Leave Logic's Reset Messages settings alone. Apple says Logic handles MIDI reset messages automatically and intelligently, so you can keep the defaults. The Control 123 (All Notes Off) and Control 121 (Reset Controls) options exist for compatibility with older MIDI devices. Switch one on only if an older synth needs it.

Source Apple — Reset Messages settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 010

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Fix doubled notes from a controller

If notes double when you record from a keyboard synth, turn Local Off on the synth. If your keyboard has no Local Off setting, use Project Settings > MIDI > General > “Instrument Without MIDI Thru Function” and choose that instrument there. When a track assigned to it is selected, Logic does not pass your controller's MIDI through, which avoids the doubled notes.

Source Apple — General MIDI project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

View settings

No. 011GAME CHANGER

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Turn on Enable Complete Features first

Go to Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced and select Enable Complete Features. It is one checkbox. Leave it off and advanced features stay hidden, including project alternatives and backups, beat mapping, and expanded mixing and automation.

Source Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 012

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Colour regions individually, not by track

Choose Logic Pro > Settings > View, click Tracks, and set the Region Color pop-up to Individual instead of As Track Color. With Individual you can colour regions independently of their track, so you can colour-code by part. With As Track Color you cannot colour regions individually.

Source Apple — Tracks View settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Color regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 013Start here

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Turn on “Show help tags”

In Logic Pro > Settings > View > General, select Show help tags. While you edit, help tags show the function name, the region or event name or number, the position and parameter values.

Source Apple — General View settings in Logic Pro for Mac

General and advanced

No. 014

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Set Auto Set Locators to By Region Selection

Control-click the Cycle button in the control bar, click Auto Set Locators and choose By Region Selection. The locators and the cycle area are then set to the borders of the selected region.

Source Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac · macProVideo — 6 Logic Pro X Cycling Tips

No. 015GAME CHANGER

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Turn on “Limit Dragging to One Direction” in the Tracks area

Tick the "Limit Dragging to One Direction: In Tracks" checkbox in Logic Pro > Settings > General > Editing. Once you start a drag left or right, movement locks to the horizontal axis, so you cannot nudge a perfectly placed region onto another track by accident. To actually change tracks, let go, reselect, and drag up or down — or hold Shift to override the limit for one move. There is a matching checkbox for the Piano Roll and Score.

Source Apple — Move regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 016

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Read the Clean Up list before you confirm it

File > Project Management > Clean Up always asks first and shows exactly what it will remove. Read the list — it deletes whole unused audio files, not just unused portions of them.

Source Apple — Clean up projects in Logic Pro for Mac

Project settings

No. 017

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Set your sample rate before you record, not after

Choose File > Project Settings > Audio and set the Sample Rate before you record or import anything. If an audio file's sample rate does not match the project's, it plays back at a different pitch. To have incoming files matched to the project rate, select "Convert audio file sample rate when importing" in File > Project Settings > Assets.

Source Apple — Set the sample rate of a project in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 018

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Set the recording bit depth in Settings > Recording

Recording bit depth is set in Logic Pro > Settings > Recording. Match it to your audio device's bit depth. With 32-bit float, files are about 33% larger than 24-bit, but you can remove clipping just by lowering the region's gain.

Source Apple — Recording settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 019GAME CHANGER

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Turn on Smart Tempo “Keep Project Tempo” by default

In File > Project Settings > Smart Tempo, set the project tempo mode to Keep Project Tempo. In Keep mode Logic Pro maintains the project tempo when you record or import audio. Adapt Project Tempo changes the project tempo to match a recording or imported file, so use it only temporarily.

Source Apple — Choose the project tempo mode in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 020

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Stop new recordings arriving pre-quantised

With no region selected, the Region inspector shows "Default Settings", and those values are applied to newly recorded regions. If new takes arrive quantised, check the Quantize value there and set it to off. Capture the performance first; quantise as a decision.

Source Apple — Use the Region inspector in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit, not re-retrieved)

No. 021

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Check Tuning when a synth sounds subtly off

Project Settings > Tuning sets the tuning for Logic's included software instruments. If a synth sounds subtly wrong against a sample, check here first: Equal Tempered turns off any alternative tuning, and the Tune slider should read A 440 Hz unless you meant to change it.

Source Apple — Tuning project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 022

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Copy your assets into the project so it travels

In File > Project Settings > Assets, select the copy checkboxes, such as "Copy audio files into project". The files are copied in the next time you save. From then on you can move or copy the project without losing any file references.

Source Apple — Manage project assets in Logic Pro for Mac

Defaults, templates and housekeeping

No. 023GAME CHANGER

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Save a Session Start template and set it as the default

Build one project with your usual tracks, buses, reverb and marker colours, then choose File > Save As Template. Then, in Project Handling settings, set the Startup Action pop-up to "Create New Project Using Default Template" and use the Default Template button to choose your template.

Source Apple — Project Handling settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 024

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Save your starting channel strip as a setting

Build one channel strip the way you always start: your go-to EQ, compressor and sends. Click the Setting button at the top of the strip, choose "Save Channel Strip Setting as", pick a folder, name it and click Save. On any new track, load it from the Setting button's pop-up menu or from the Library.

Source Apple — Work with channel strip settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 025

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Give each colour a fixed meaning

Press ⌥C to open the Color palette (or Control-click a region and choose Name and Color > Show/Hide Colors), then click a colour. Decide once what each colour means to you (drums, vocals, keys, reference) and colour your template that way, so every project opens with the same language.

Source Apple — Color regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 026

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Make a Project Alternative before big changes

File > Project Alternatives > New Alternative gives you another version of the project: name it and click Done. Make one before every big arrangement change. Alternatives need Enable Complete Features in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced. File > Project Alternatives > Edit Alternatives lets you rename or delete them; you can't remove the Main alternative.

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 027Start here

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Hit ⌘S often: every save banks a backup

Each time you save with File > Save (⌘S), Logic keeps a backup of the current project alternative, up to ten per alternative. To go back, choose File > Revert to and pick one; they're listed newest first. Backups need Enable Complete Features. Build the reflex of hitting ⌘S every time you finish a thought.

⌘S

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Advanced settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 028

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Move the Sound Library to an external drive on purpose

Logic Pro > Sound Library > Relocate Sound Library moves the library off your system drive: pick the drive or volume and click Relocate. Afterwards, don't rename that drive, or Logic Pro won't be able to find the Sound Library.

Source Apple Support - Relocate the Sound Library (from prior audit, not re-retrieved)

No. 029

Section 01 · Setting Up Logic

Save the project as a Package so it travels

In the File > Save As dialog, choose "Organize my project as: Package" to save the project as a single file (package) containing its assets. Assets saved in the project are still there when you move or copy it. Choose Folder instead if you want a project folder with subfolders for each asset type.

Source Apple — Save Logic Pro for Mac projects

Section 02 · 14 tricks

Arrangement Tricks.

Arranging is mostly moving big blocks of time around without breaking anything. These tricks let you restructure a whole song without dragging regions one by one.

Moving time, not regions

No. 030Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Use the Arrangement track to move whole sections

Open Global Tracks with G, enable the Arrangement track, and drop markers on your Verse, Chorus and Bridge. Now drag the Chorus marker and the entire section — every track, every automation point — moves with it.

G

Source Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 031Start here

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Drag one arrangement marker onto another to swap sections

Drag one arrangement marker directly over another and the two switch places, with all their content swapped. Every region, marker and automation point in each section goes with it, so you can try several song orders in moments.

Source Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 032Start here

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

⌥‑drag an arrangement marker to duplicate a section

Hold ⌥ and drag any arrangement marker to copy that entire section, contents and all, to a new point in the timeline.

⌥ + drag

Source Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 033Start here

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Delete a section and close the gap

Select the arrangement marker and press Delete once — that removes the section's regions. Press Delete again and the marker goes too, pulling everything after it back to close the hole.

Source Apple — Edit arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 034

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Insert silence between the locators

Set the locators around the gap you want, then choose Edit > Cut/Insert Time > Insert Silence Between Locators. A region that crosses the left locator is cut there, and the part after it moves to the right of the right locator. It's a quick way to add two bars to an intro.

Source macProVideo — Making Whole Project Edits in Logic Pro · 9to5Mac — Logic Pros: One-click Logic arrangement tricks · Apple — Add or remove gaps in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 035

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Resize arrangement markers to fit your sections

New arrangement markers always appear at the start of the project or after the last existing marker, eight bars long, regardless of the playhead position. So create the marker first, then drag its right edge left or right until it matches the section.

Source Apple — Add arrangement markers in Logic Pro for Mac

Building and duplicating

No. 036

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Use aliases for parts that must stay identical

Option-Shift-drag a MIDI region to where you want the alias to start. An alias is a reference to the original region, so when you change the original, every alias changes too. Use it for a part that has to repeat identically across the song.

⌥⇧ + drag

Source macProVideo — Understanding Aliases in Logic Pro · Apple — Create MIDI aliases in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 037

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Make a folder out of a section

Select every region in a section and choose Functions > Folder > Pack Folder from the Tracks area menu bar to pack them into a folder.

Source Apple — Pack and unpack folders in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 038Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Colour‑code sections, not instruments

Open the colour palette with ⌥C and give every chorus the same colour across all tracks. You can then read the arrangement at a glance from fully zoomed out.

⌥C

Source Apple — Change the color of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

Judging the arrangement

No. 039

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Use Track Stacks to collapse instrument families

Select related tracks, create a Track Stack and choose Summing Stack. All the tracks in a summing stack send their audio to one shared auxiliary track, so a whole drum kit sits under a single stack.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac track stacks overview · Logic Studio Training — How To Organize Your Logic Pro Projects With Folder Track Stacks

No. 040

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Loop an arrangement section with one key

Select the regions that make up the section and press U (Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events and Enable Cycle). Logic sets the locators around your selection, rounded to the nearest barlines, and turns Cycle on, so the section loops in time. Press ⌘U instead to set the locators exactly at the selection's edges.

U

Source macProVideo — 6 Logic Pro X Cycling Tips For A Faster Production Workflow · studio-interns.com — Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events (keyboard command of the day) · studio-interns.com — Set Locators/Loop by Regions/Events/Marquee and Enable Cycle/Loop ⌘U

No. 041Start here

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Mute regions instead of deleting them while experimenting

Click a region with the Mute tool, or select the regions and press Control-M. Muted regions turn grey with a dot before the name, so arrangement experiments become reversible without touching undo.

⌃M

Source Apple — Mute and solo regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 042Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Keep a “graveyard” track at the bottom

Make one muted, hidden track and drag every rejected idea onto it. Nothing is ever deleted, and the good version of that rejected idea is there when you need it three weeks later.

No. 043

Section 02 · Arrangement Tricks

Use markers for notes to self, not just sections

The Marker track is one of the global tracks shown by default. Create a marker, then rename it “fix snare here” or “vocal comp needed”. Your to‑do list lives on the timeline instead of on paper.

Source Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Rename markers in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 03 · 5 tricks

Navigating Tricks.

Getting the playhead and the view where you want them, instantly, is the difference between working and fiddling.

Getting around

No. 044Start here

Section 03 · Navigating Tricks

Drag‑zoom to any area with ⌃⌥

Hold ⌃⌥ and drag a box around any part of the arrangement to zoom straight to it. Hold ⌃⌥ and click empty space to zoom back out.

⌃⌥ + drag

Source Apple — Zoom windows in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 045

Section 03 · Navigating Tricks

Know what the number keys actually do

The number keys recall screensets, not markers — Apple's guide says you recall a screenset by pressing any numeric key except 0, so 1–9 switch window layouts. If you want marker jumps on a key, open Key Commands (⌥K) and search “Go to Marker Number” — there are 20 of them, numbered by the order the markers appear in the project.

Source Apple — Create and recall screensets in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Navigate using markers in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 046

Section 03 · Navigating Tricks

Scroll without the scrollbar

If your Mac has a trackpad that supports gestures, you can scroll and zoom the Tracks area with gestures instead of reaching for the scrollbars. On a Mac with a Touch Bar, swipe left or right on the Touch Bar to scroll through the visible area of the project.

Source Apple — Scroll and zoom in the Tracks area in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 047

Section 03 · Navigating Tricks

Use the Cycle area as a bookmark

Select the region or passage you are working on and press U (Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events and Enable Cycle). Logic sets the left and right locators around the selection, rounded, and turns Cycle on, so the cycle area marks your work area. Use ⌘U instead if you want the locators set by the selection without rounding.

U

Source Apple — Key commands for Global Commands in Logic Pro for Mac · studio-interns.com — Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events (keyboard command of the day) · studio-interns.com — Set Locators/Loop by Regions/Events/Marquee and Enable Cycle/Loop ⌘U · afteraudio.com — Key commands for Global Commands in Logic Pro

No. 048

Section 03 · Navigating Tricks

Toggle Catch to stop the screen running away

With Catch on, the visible section of a window follows the playhead during playback. For detailed editing, click the Catch button in the Tracks area (or editor) menu bar to turn it off, and the view holds still. If it keeps switching back on, check Logic Pro > Settings > General > Catch: “Catch when starting playback” and “Catch when moving playhead” re-enable it.

Source Apple — Control windows using Catch modes in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Catch settings in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 04 · 13 tricks

Composing MIDI Tricks.

Getting ideas out of your head and into the sequencer before they evaporate. These tricks are about speed of capture first and correctness second — you can always fix it later, but you cannot un‑forget an idea.

Capture without a keyboard

No. 049Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Capture the last thing you played, even when not recording

If you played something great without recording, press ⇧R (Flashback Capture) and Logic turns it into a region. MIDI can be captured whether the project is playing or stopped. Audio capture arrived in Logic 11.2: give the audio track focus and play the project. Logic saves audio only while there is an incoming signal, needs at least four seconds of playback, and keeps up to one minute.

⇧R

Source Apple — Capture a recent audio performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Capture your most recent MIDI performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — What's new in Logic Pro for Mac 11.2 · Logic Studio Training — Logic Pro 11.2 Update: Flashback Recording

No. 050Start here

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Use the Step Input Keyboard for parts you cannot play

Choose Window > Show Step Input Keyboard to enter notes one at a time, setting each note's length and velocity with the Note Length and Velocity buttons.

Source Apple — Use step input recording techniques in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 051Start here

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Draw notes with the Pencil, delete with the Eraser

The Pencil creates a note whose length, velocity and MIDI channel match the last note you created or edited. To remove a note, select it and press Delete, or click it with the Eraser tool. ⌥-drag a note to copy it to a new position.

Source Apple — Add notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Delete notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Copy notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

Chords, scales and harmony

No. 052GAME CHANGER

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Use the Chord Trigger MIDI plugin to play chords with one finger

Insert Chord Trigger in the MIDI FX slot and click Learn. Click the trigger key you want on the upper keyboard first, then click the notes of the chord on the lower keyboard, then click Learn again to finish. Whole progressions become one-finger performances.

Source Apple — Use Chord Trigger in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Chord Trigger overview in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 053

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Force everything into key with Transposer

Insert the Transposer MIDI FX and set its Root and Scale pop-up menus. Transposer transposes incoming MIDI notes in real time and corrects them to the selected scale, so you stay in key as you play. Choose User and click notes off on the on-screen keyboard to build your own scale.

Source Apple — Transposer in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 054

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Use Arpeggiator to generate parts, then commit them

Insert Arpeggiator and dial in a pattern, then commit it with Bounce in Place. Logic renders the selected region, including all active plug-ins and automation data, to a 24-bit audio file at the project sample rate. The live pattern becomes a fixed part you can edit as audio.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview · Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 055

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Transpose without touching the notes

Select the regions and change Transpose in the Region inspector. Region parameters affect how regions play back but don't alter the data inside them, and every selected region changes together. If the project is playing, you hear the change immediately, so you can audition a new key and set it back to zero if it doesn't work.

Source Apple — Use the Region inspector in Logic Pro for Mac · Logic Studio Training — Master Region Editing with Logic Pro's Inspector Tools · Apple — Logic Pro MIDI region parameters (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 056

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Use the Modifier MIDI plugin to reassign a controller

The Modifier MIDI plug-in reassigns or filters a single continuous controller or fader event. Choose or learn the incoming type in Input Event and the outgoing type in Re-Assign To, then use the Scale and Add sliders to scale or offset the output values.

Source Apple — Modifier in Logic Pro for Mac

Working fast while ideas are hot

No. 057

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Merge cycle takes to layer a part pass by pass

To build up a drum pattern one element per pass, set MIDI cycle recording to Merge: each pass of the cycle adds to the same region.

Source Apple — Recording settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 058

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Freeze the instrument as soon as the part is done

Freeze the software instrument track once the part is done. Logic renders its instrument and effect plug-ins so they stop costing CPU, and unlike Bounce in Place, Freeze lets you return to the original track and its automation more easily. The trade-off: Apple notes that frozen instrument tracks can put more load on your disk, so if disk overload alerts start appearing, that is the likely cause.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview · Apple — Freeze tracks in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 059

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Commit a MIDI region to audio with Bounce in Place

Select the MIDI region and use Bounce in Place. Logic renders it through the instrument and all active plug-ins, plus automation data, to a 24-bit audio region at the project sample rate, which locks the idea in as audio.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview · Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 060

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Keep one “sketch” instrument track loaded at all times

Keep a piano patch on a permanently armed track so any idea can be captured right away. The moment capture takes effort, ideas stop arriving.

No. 061

Section 04 · Composing MIDI Tricks

Use Note Repeat for hi‑hats and rolls

In Step Sequencer, choose Note Repeat from the Edit Mode selector, then drag up on a hi-hat step to slice it into more repeats (1 to 16) or down for fewer. The inspector adds velocity ramp, velocity curve and Distribution for each step, so a roll can accelerate or decelerate instead of sitting flat.

Source Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 05 · 13 tricks

Piano Roll Tricks.

The Piano Roll is where MIDI becomes music. These are the editing moves that make it fast.

Selecting notes intelligently

No. 062Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Select all notes of the same pitch in one click

Click a key on the keyboard graphic at the left of the Piano Roll and every note at that pitch in the region is selected. Perfect for grabbing all the hi‑hats at once.

Source Apple — Select notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Editing notes

No. 063GAME CHANGER

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Change note length numerically in the Event Float

Open the Event Float window with Window > Show Event Float, or press ⌥E. It shows the selected note as one line in the same format as the Event List, and you can type new values straight in, length included.

⌥E

Source Apple — Use the Event Float window in Logic Pro for Mac · Studio Interns — Show/Hide Event Float ⌥E, Logic Pro keyboard command of the day · Logic Pro GEM — Fader Event: A MIDI Event Wannabe

No. 064

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Force legato to fix gappy pads

Select the notes, then choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Following Notes (Force Legato) in the Piano Roll. Every note extends to end where the next one begins, and pads and basslines stop sounding stuttery instantly.

Source 9to5Mac — The Logic Pros: 3 helpful tricks to streamline your MIDI/audio editing · Your Local Musician — Logic Pro X Tutorial: Force Legato · Apple — Resize notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 065

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Trim overlaps automatically

Select the notes and choose Edit > Trim > Note End to Remove Overlaps to Following Notes (8 Ticks Gap) in the Piano Roll. Logic shortens the note ends so nothing overlaps, leaving an eight-tick gap before the next note. A Selected Notes version does the same job measured only against the other selected notes.

Source Apple — Resize notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 066

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

⌥‑drag a note to duplicate it

Hold ⌥ while dragging any note or selection to copy rather than move — you can even ⌥-drag notes between two Piano Roll windows, or between two different projects. To stop a drag changing pitch, turn on Logic Pro > Settings > General > Editing > "Limit Dragging to One Direction In Piano Roll and Score": the direction you start in is then the only one you can move in. Pressing ⇧ while dragging switches that behaviour on and off; it is not a pitch lock on its own. Apple's Logic Pro 12.2 release notes list a fix for Piano Roll notes not honoring this setting when dragged, so update if it seems to be ignored.

⌥ + drag

Source Apple — Copy notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

No. 067

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Place a note between grid divisions

Set the Snap pop-up menu to Ticks, which snaps to 1/3840 of a beat, or press Control-Shift as you drag to move the note in tick steps, overriding the Snap value. You can also switch snapping off with the On/Off button beside the Snap pop-up menu.

⌃⇧ + drag

Source Apple — Snap items to the grid in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Move notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

Velocity and expression

No. 068GAME CHANGER

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Change velocity by dragging with the Velocity tool

Pick the Velocity tool from the Tool menu, or hold Control-Command to turn the Pointer into it temporarily, then drag up or down on a note. A help tag shows the velocity as you drag. Choose View > Set Note Color > By Velocity if you want the note colour to track it too.

⌃⌘ (hold)

Source Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 069

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Change a selection's velocity without flattening it

Select the notes, then drag one of them vertically with the Velocity tool, or drag the Velocity slider in the Piano Roll header. Logic keeps the relative differences between the notes' velocities. When any note hits 0 or 127, the rest stop too. Hold ⌥ while dragging to override this.

Source Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 070

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Show the automation lane inside the Piano Roll

Click the Show/Hide Automation button in the Piano Roll Editor menu bar, then choose a parameter from the Automation/MIDI Parameter pop-up menu. Its MIDI or automation data appears in a lane under the notes, where you can edit it. Track automation shown there is the same curve as in the Tracks area, so edits appear in both places.

Source Apple — The Automation/MIDI area in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 071

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Colour notes by velocity to read dynamics instantly

In the Piano Roll's View menu, set note colour to Velocity. Flat parts become visibly, obviously flat.

Source Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

Quantise and timing

No. 072GAME CHANGER

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Quantise from the region inspector, not destructively

The Quantize field in the Region inspector is non‑destructive and can be dialled back or removed at any point. Use it before you ever use the destructive version.

Source Apple — Quantize parameter values in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 073

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Use Q‑Strength to keep the human feel

Under the region's more‑options triangle, Q‑Strength at 60 to 80 percent pulls notes toward the grid without gluing them to it.

Source Apple — Advanced quantization parameters in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 074

Section 05 · Piano Roll Tricks

Quantise only the notes that need it

Select the offending notes in the Piano Roll and quantise the selection rather than the whole region. The good parts of the take stay untouched.

Source Apple — Quantize the timing of notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Section 06 · 12 tricks

Recording Audio Tricks.

These tricks are about getting a clean, usable, well‑organised take the first time, and not losing a good performance to a technical mistake.

Before you hit record

No. 075

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Aim your peaks at −12 to −18 dBFS

Aim for your loudest peaks to land between −12 and −18 dBFS. In 24-bit, recording hot won't improve the real-world noise performance. It just makes the track harder to mix against others recorded with sensible headroom.

Source Sound On Sound — Q. How much headroom should I leave with 24-bit recording? · Sound On Sound — Q. Should I gain-stage to -6dBFS or -18dBFS?

No. 076GAME CHANGER

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Track at the lowest I/O buffer your Mac can handle

Set the buffer before tracking, not during. In Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > Devices, choose the lowest I/O Buffer Size your Mac can handle. If you get system overload alerts, step it up one setting. Logic shows the resulting latency under the I/O Buffer Size menu, so judge by that readout, not the sample number.

Source Apple — Manage input monitoring latency in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 077

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Turn on Low Latency Monitoring mode instead of disabling plug-ins one by one

Low Latency Monitoring mode bypasses the latency-inducing plug-ins that push a track past the Limit slider in Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > General (up to 30 ms). It also turns off that track's Aux sends, which kills a headphone reverb fed from a send. It affects only the focused instrument track and tracks with Input Monitoring or Record Enable on.

Source Apple — Work with plug-in latencies in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 078

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Count-in and pre-roll are either/or — pick the right one

In the Recording project settings, the When Beginning buttons make you choose a count-in or a pre-roll. Count-in is set in bars or beats. Pre-roll is a playback time in seconds, up to 60. Use pre-roll when bars mean nothing (free-tempo material, dialogue) and count-in when you want the performer counted in musically.

Source Apple — Recording project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 079Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Name the track before you record, always

Regions that use the track name as their region name, and their source audio files, follow a default track name like “Audio 3”. That name means nothing to you three months later.

Source Apple — Rename tracks in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit; not re-retrieved this session)

No. 080Start here

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Record‑enable multiple tracks at once

Click the Record Enable button in the track header of each track you want to record to — every armed button blinks red. Option-click is the escape hatch, not the shortcut: Option-clicking a track's Record Enable button makes it the only record-ready track, and Option-clicking a track that is already blinking red clears record-ready status across the whole project. Learn it as "solo the arm" and "disarm everything".

Source Apple — Record to multiple audio tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

While recording

No. 081Start here

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

⌘. discards the take you just recorded

Press ⌘. — Discard Recording and Return to Last Play Position — to stop and throw away the take you just recorded, for when you know instantly it was not the one.

⌘.

Source Apple — Advanced recording commands in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 082

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Watch the take list, not the waveform

The Take Folder pop-up menu in the upper-left corner of a take folder lists every take you've banked, and you can pick one from it during playback. If the performer is on take 14 and getting worse, that list is your cue to stop and move on.

Source Apple — Preview take recordings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

Monitoring and headphones

No. 083GAME CHANGER

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Build a dedicated headphone mix on a bus

Select every channel strip, choose a bus in a Send slot, and route the aux channel strip Logic creates to the output that feeds the headphone amp. Give the performer more of themselves and more reverb than you would ever put in the mix. Comfort produces better takes than accuracy does.

Source Apple — Send a mix to multiple destinations in Logic Pro for Mac (from prior audit; not re-retrieved this session)

No. 084

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Use Input Monitoring rather than record enable to rehearse

The Input Monitoring (I) button in the track header lets you hear a track that isn't record-enabled, so you can set levels and practise the part before committing. On audio tracks it still involves some latency, depending on your hardware and driver settings.

Source Apple — Use input monitoring with tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 085

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Turn off Software Monitoring when your interface can monitor

Software monitoring always carries some delay. Apple's advice when your interface supports hardware monitoring: turn off Software monitoring in Logic Pro > Settings > Audio > General, or with its control bar button.

Source Apple — General Audio settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Work with plug-in latencies in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 086Start here

Section 06 · Recording Audio Tricks

Give the performer a click they can feel

Swap the metronome sound, add a bar accent, or better, program a simple drum loop. A musical reference beats a woodblock every time.

Source Apple — Metronome project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 07 · 6 tricks

Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI.

The everyday editing moves in the Tracks area: selecting, trimming, splitting, joining and moving regions.

Universal region commands

No. 087

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

Trim to the playhead from either direction

The commands are “Set Region/Event/Marquee Start to Playhead Position” and the matching End command — search the Key Commands window for “Playhead Position” and put them on keys. (Note that on audio regions the Start command also moves the region anchor to the playhead.) Related one-shot trims live under Edit > Trim, such as Region End to Next Region. No mouse precision needed.

Source Apple — Resize regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac · Studio Interns — Trim Region End to Next Region

Snap, grid and precision

No. 088

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

Use Snap Regions to Relative Value for off-grid parts

By default, Logic's Snap menu is set to Snap Regions to Absolute Value: a moved item snaps exactly to the nearest grid position. For a region that sits deliberately off-grid, choose Snap > Snap Regions to Relative Value in the Tracks area menu bar. It keeps its distance from the grid: a region at 2.1.1.16 moved one beat forward lands on 2.2.1.16, not 2.2.1.1.

Source Apple — Snap items to the grid in Logic Pro for Mac

Tools and selection

No. 089Start here

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

T opens the Tool menu, T again closes it

Press T to open the Tool menu at the pointer — Apple's default key command for Show Tool Menu. Press T again to close it.

T

Source Apple — Key commands for Tool Menu in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Overview of tools in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 090

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

⌘ is your secondary tool

Logic has two Tool menus: Left-click and Command-click. Choose a tool from the Command-click Tool menu, then hold ⌘ to use it. Let go and you are back on your Left-click tool. The Command-click Tool menu only appears when Enable Complete Features is on, in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced.

Source Apple — Overview of tools in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Assign tools in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Use the complete set of features in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 091Start here

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

Select everything after this point in one keystroke

Press ⇧F (Select All Following) to select everything that comes after the current selection. That puts you one keystroke from moving the rest of the song.

⇧F

Source Apple — Key commands for Main Window Tracks and Various Editors in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Select events in the Logic Pro for Mac Event List · studio-interns.com — Select All Following ⇧F · studio-interns.com — Select All Following of Same Track/Pitch ⌃⇧F

No. 092

Section 07 · Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI

Lock events so tempo changes cannot move them

Lock SMPTE Position keeps events at their absolute time when you change the tempo later. In the Event List, select events and choose Functions > Lock SMPTE Position, or Control-click and choose it from the shortcut menu; a padlock appears in the Lock column. Lock a region and every event inside it is locked. It requires Enable Complete Features in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced.

Source Apple — Protect the position of events in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 08 · 15 tricks

Audio Editing Tricks.

Comping, crossfades, timing and pitch — where a good take becomes a great one.

Comping takes

No. 093

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Put take-switching on keys you choose

Press ⌥K to open the Key Commands window and type “Take” in the search field. Find Select Previous Take or Comp and Select Next Take or Comp, which step through the takes and comps listed in the take folder’s pop-up menu. Check what they are assigned to, and put them on keys you can reach while you audition.

⌥K

Source Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Preview take recordings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 094

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Save your comp as a new comp before changing it

The take folder menu has “Duplicate Comp”. Do this before every significant change and you can always go back to the version that was working.

Source Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 095

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Move a comp edit point without redoing the comp

Drag the vertical divider between two take sections to slide the edit point earlier or later.

Source Apple — Edit comps in Logic Pro for Mac

Fades and clicks

No. 096

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Curve the fade after you draw it

With the Fade tool, hover over the middle of a fade you've made and drag left or right to change its curve. Or select the region and adjust the fade's Curve value in the Region inspector.

Source Why Logic Pro Rules - How to Get the Most Out of Logic Pro X's Fade Tool · Apple — Edit fades in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 097GAME CHANGER

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Use “Remove Silence from Audio Region” on a live kit or spoken word

Select the audio region and press ⌃X (Remove Silence from Audio Region). Everything below a threshold you set is removed, and new regions are created from what remains. That makes it useful for a live kit or spoken word.

⌃X

Source studio-interns.com — Remove Silence from Audio Region… ⌃X · 9to5Mac — Editing noisy audio files with Remove Silence in Logic Pro X · Apple — Uses for Remove Silence in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 098

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Stop clicks at region starts with a short fade

Audio that starts abruptly can click. A short fade-in gives it a gradual ramp and prevents the click. When you trim or split in the Audio Track Editor, turn on Snap to Zero Crossings as well, so the edit lands where no click is produced.

Source Why Logic Pro Rules — How to Get the Most Out of Logic Pro X's Fade Tool · Apple — Snap to zero in the Logic Pro for Mac Audio Track Editor

Timing and pitch

No. 099

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Add flex markers either side before you move one

Placing anchor markers on the neighbouring transients stops your edit from stretching the whole bar.

Source Apple — Flex tool time stretching in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 100

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Quantise audio with Flex enabled

Give the audio track a Flex mode and make sure Flex is selected for the region in the Region inspector. You can then quantize that audio by choosing a value from the Quantize pop-up menu in the Region inspector. It's real-time, so you can change the value later, or turn it off to get the original timing back.

Source macProVideo - Quantizing In Logic: The Essentials · Sound On Sound - Logic Pro: Editing Drum Timings · Apple — Quantize regions in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 101

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Use Flex Pitch to fix a single flat note

Switch the track's Flex mode to Flex Pitch, then drag the note blob vertically. The gain, vibrato, pitch drift and formant handles are all on the same blob.

Source Apple — Edit pitch and timing with Flex Pitch in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 102

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Reset all Flex edits rather than undoing repeatedly

Control-click the flexed region and choose Reset All Flex Edits. It clears the region's flex data and starts you fresh.

Source Apple — Delete, reset and move flex markers in Logic Pro for Mac

Destructive and file‑level editing

No. 103

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Use the Audio File Editor for true destructive edits

Double‑click a region and switch to the File tab. Silence, reverse, normalise and pencil‑edit at the sample level. Changes here affect the file itself.

Source Apple — Audio File Editor overview in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 104

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Change region level non‑destructively with Gain

The Region inspector's Gain parameter changes playback level without touching the file. Always try this before normalising.

Source Apple — Change gain of audio regions in the Tracks area (Logic Pro for Mac)

No. 105

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Reclaim disk space with Project Management > Clean Up

Once your comps are final, choose File > Project Management > Clean Up. Its options are Delete Unused Audio Files, Delete Unreferenced Audio Files and Delete Backups, and files are deleted from disk. A dialog lists everything to be deleted, so deselect the Delete checkbox for anything you want to keep, and back up first.

Source Apple — Clean up Logic Pro for Mac projects · Apple — Remove unused audio files in your Logic Pro for Mac project

No. 106

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Reverse a region, destructively or not

Select the region, then Functions > Reverse in the Audio File Editor, or apply the Reverse setting in the region inspector for a non‑destructive version.

Source Apple — Reverse audio regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 107

Section 08 · Audio Editing Tricks

Commit edits with Bounce Regions in Place

When you are happy with a comp, select the regions and choose File > Bounce > Regions in Place. In the dialog, set the name and a Destination: New Track, or Selected Track to replace the regions. Set Source to Leave, Mute or Delete, and decide whether to Bypass Effect Plug-ins. Choose Leave or Mute to keep the original.

Source Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 09 · 6 tricks

Marquee Tool Tricks.

The Marquee tool selects a range of time rather than whole regions, across one track or many. Once that clicks, a lot of editing you would otherwise do by hand becomes unnecessary.

Source Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

The essentials

No. 108Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 09 · Marquee Tool Tricks

Make Marquee your ⌘-click tool

Make Marquee your Command-click tool. In the Tracks area, click the Command-click Tool menu and choose the Marquee tool. From then on, hold ⌘ and drag to marquee-select parts of regions on one or more tracks. Release ⌘ and you're back on your Left-click tool. The Command-click Tool menu only appears when Enable Complete Features is on, in Logic Pro > Settings > Advanced.

⌘ + drag

Start playback while a marquee selection is active and Logic plays from the selection's left edge to its right edge, then stops. It's the fastest way to audition a specific range without touching the locators.

With automation showing, drag a marquee across part of an automation lane, then click inside the selection. Drag in the marquee ruler across the bar before a chorus to select it on every track, then delete. You get clean, arrangement-wide silence for that bar in one edit.

Section 10 · 13 tricks

Automation Tricks.

Automation is what separates a static mix from a moving one. Logic has two kinds: track automation stays tied to its place on the timeline, while region automation travels with its region. Knowing which one you are in explains most automation surprises.

Source Apple — Track automation vs. region automation in Logic Pro for Mac

The two systems

No. 114

Section 10 · Automation Tricks

Use Region automation for anything that belongs to the part

A filter sweep that is part of a synth riff should move with the riff. Region automation does that; track automation does not.

Source Apple — Track automation vs region automation in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 115Start here

Section 10 · Automation Tricks

Press A to toggle automation view

Press A to show or hide track automation. In the Audio Track Editor it does the same job as the Show/Hide Automation button.

A

Writing automation

No. 116GAME CHANGER

Section 10 · Automation Tricks

Use Latch mode for almost everything

Latch writes while you move the control and holds the last value when you let go. Touch snaps back, Write erases as it goes, and Read plays only. Latch is the right default.

Source Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 117

Section 10 · Automation Tricks

Never leave a track in Write mode

Write mode erases existing automation as the playhead passes, whether you touch the fader or not.

Source Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 118Start here

Delete an automation point without dragging it

Double-click the point, or select it and press Delete, or drag across it with the Eraser.

Curve an automation line with ⌃⇧-drag

Hold ⌃⇧ and, with the Pointer tool, drag the line between two automation points to bend it into a curve. This works as long as the two points aren't directly above each other.

⌃⇧ + drag

Section 10 · Automation Tricks

Trim existing automation up or down

Trim is not a mode on its own. It works in combination with Touch or Latch. With it on, moving the fader offsets existing automation up or down by the amount you move it. It applies only to Volume, Pan and Send levels, so use it to lift an already-automated vocal without redrawing its moves.

Source Apple — Choose automation modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 121

Use Relative mode to layer a second pass

Relative automation sits on top of your existing pass as an offset, so you can add a ride without destroying the original moves.

Marquee a range, then drag the line to change only that section

Drag across the bars you want to change with the Marquee tool, then drag the automation line inside that selection. Logic creates two automation points at the left edge and two at the right edge of the selection, so the change stays boxed in and does not bleed into the surrounding bars.

Show several automation lanes at once

Instead of switching one automation curve between parameters, show automation sub-lanes, which appear below the main track. Click the automation sub-lane disclosure triangle, then choose each lane's parameter from its Automation Parameter pop-up menu. You can then see several parameters at once.

Automation can become orphaned when it is copied between tracks.

Thin dense automation after recording a controller pass

Delete Redundant Automation Points cleans up heavy controller passes, but it is global: it removes redundant points on all regions and all tracks, not just your selection. To thin one passage only, select the points in that range and press Delete, then redraw.

Open the Snap pop-up menu in the Tracks area, choose Snap Automation, and pick a value from the submenu. Automation edits then snap to that value, so filter stabs land on the grid. You can set it independently in the Tracks area and the Piano Roll Editor.

Section 11 · 11 tricks

Step Sequencer Tricks.

The Step Sequencer is more than a drum grid. Each row can have its own length, step rate, playback mode and start offset, so rows can drift against each other in ways a fixed grid never will.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac

The basics done right

No. 127GAME CHANGER

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Give every row a different step rate

Rows do not have to share the pattern's step rate. Click a row header to select the row, then in the Step Sequencer inspector click Row and choose a note value from the Step Rate pop-up menu. To change just one step, switch to Step Rate edit mode and drag vertically in that step. Hats at 1/16 and kick at 1/8 each run at their own speed.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit Step Sequencer rows in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Change the musical length of a pattern in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 128

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Use the row's Playback Mode for variation

Forward, Backward, Ping-Pong, Pendulum, Wander, Shuffle and Random: set one for the whole pattern, or a different one per row. Set just the hats to Random and their step order becomes completely random and nonlooping while the kick stays put.

Source Apple — Modify pattern playback in Step Sequencer in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 129

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Increase pattern length beyond 16 steps

The Step Sequencer supports up to 64 steps per pattern. Longer patterns mean fewer copies and more room for fills.

Source Apple — Change the musical length of a pattern in Logic Pro for Mac

Per‑step editing

No. 130

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Use Note Repeat for rolls without drawing them

Set a step's repeat value to 4 and it fires four times inside that step. Instant trap hats, no extra steps required.

Source Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 131

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Use Gate to shorten hits and Tie to lengthen them

Gate sets a step's note length as a percentage of the step, shortening it to less than the step's full duration — short gates on a bass pattern give you staccato stabs. It only ever shortens; to make a note run longer than its step, switch to Tie edit mode and click the right edge of the step to tie it to the following one, which lengthens its duration by the value of the step it is tied to. Both are per-step, not per-pattern.

Source Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 132

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Tie steps together for sustained notes

Tie mode joins consecutive steps into one long note, which is how you write bass and lead lines rather than just percussion.

Source Apple — Use Step Sequencer edit modes in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 133

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Clear a step to reset all its edit-mode values

Over-edited a step? Shift-click it to select it, then choose Functions > Clear Step from the Step Sequencer menu bar. That resets all of the step's edit-mode values to their defaults in one move — for step rate, the default is the row's step rate. You can also clear a whole row or the whole pattern.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer steps in Logic Pro for Mac

Beyond drums

No. 134

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Use the Step Sequencer on any software instrument

It is not a drum tool. Put it on a synth, switch the rows to pitches, and you have a hardware‑style note sequencer.

Source Apple — Overview of Step Sequencer in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 135GAME CHANGER

Automate plugin parameters per step

Add a row and assign it to any automatable plugin parameter. Now you can sequence filter cutoff step by step alongside the notes.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer rows in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 136

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Build a library of pattern regions

Save patterns through the Pattern Browser, or keep a muted track of favourites at the bottom of a template project.

Source Apple — Load and save patterns in Step Sequencer in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 137

Section 11 · Step Sequencer Tricks

Use Skip and Loop Start/End to reshape a row

Skip drops a step from playback: the sequencer moves straight to the next step, which shortens the row by that step's length. Loop Start/End sets where the row cycles.

Logic Drummer Tricks.

Drummer is not a loop library. It plays a performance you can steer, and its kick and snare can follow the rhythm of another track in your project — a different one for each region if you like.

Use Complexity and Intensity, then the kit-piece sliders

In the Session Player Editor, drag the Complexity slider up for a busier part and the Intensity slider up for a louder one. Apple lists both as settings common to all Session Players, Drummer included. Then click Details and drag the kit piece sliders to set the complexity range of individual kit pieces.

Change the drummer, not just the preset

If a preset is close but the feel is wrong, try other presets or drummers. Lock the fills first if you like them: Apple says the lock stops 'any changes to the fills setting when switching presets or drummers.'

Turn individual kit pieces on and off per region

Click a kit piece in the editor to enable or disable it for that region only. Drop the crash out of the verse and back in for the chorus.

In Drum Kit Designer, click a kit piece to open its Edit and Exchange panes. Swap the kick or snare (toms, cymbals and hi-hat too on multi-channel kits) and set Tune, Dampen (sustain) and Gain per piece. Multi-channel kits add Overheads and Room (A, B or off) switches.

Section 13 · 6 tricks

Drum Machine Designer Tricks.

Drum Machine Designer is built on a Track Stack: every pad you fill gets its own subtrack and channel strip, so each drum sound can be processed on its own in the Mixer.

Building the kit

Drag any audio file straight onto a pad

Drag a WAV, AIFF or MP3 from the Finder or a Logic Pro browser, or a region from the Tracks area, onto a pad to add it to your kit. When you drop a region onto a pad, Drum Machine Designer inserts a new Quick Sampler instance on a new subtrack.

Use Pad Controls for quick shaping

Select a pad and click Pad Controls in the bar below the grid. The pad's tone and effect parameters appear in the Plug-in pane. A Drum Machine Designer kit is a track stack. Plug-ins on its main track affect every subtrack, so put your kit compressor and limiter there. Any pad whose output you route outside the stack skips that processing.

Section 14 · 7 tricks

Quick Sampler Tricks.

Quick Sampler turns any sound into a playable instrument — the short route from “that noise is interesting” to “that noise is now a bassline”.

Loading and slicing

No. 150

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Know the four modes and pick deliberately

Classic plays the sample while you hold a key, the way to play a sound across the keyboard. One Shot plays from start marker to end marker on each note, good for drum loops and effects. Slice chops a sample into slices mapped to keys. Recorder captures live input as an audio recording.

Source Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 151GAME CHANGER

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Use Slice mode with Transient detection on any break

Load a drum loop, switch to Slice, choose Transient from the Mode pop-up menu, and each slice is mapped to its own key. Drag from the lower part of the waveform display to a software instrument track in the Tracks area to get the MIDI — the original groove, fully rearrangeable.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler Slice mode in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 152

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Drag audio directly from the Tracks area into a loaded Quick Sampler

Drag a region into Quick Sampler's waveform display to swap the sound. Drop it on Original to keep the file's own tuning, loudness, looping and length. Drop it on Optimized and Quick Sampler optimizes tuning, loudness and length, and adds loop and crossfade markers to rhythmic or looped material. The region is bounced offline first. Dragging to the track header instead opens the Replace existing sound dialog.

Source Apple — Add audio to Quick Sampler in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Drag and drop to create sampler instrument tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

Shaping the sound

No. 153

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Use Flex and Follow Tempo to lock a loop to the project

Flex and Follow Tempo are separate buttons at the lower right of the waveform display in Classic, One Shot and Slice modes. Flex alone plays the sample at its original speed on every key: the pitch changes, the speed doesn't. Turn on Follow Tempo as well and playback syncs to the project tempo, with slices stretching or contracting to match.

Source Apple — Use Flex in Quick Sampler in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 154

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Set the root key correctly or nothing will be in tune

The root key is the note that plays your sample at its original pitch; keys above and below transpose it up or down. If a sample plays out of tune across the keyboard, open the Pitch controls and set the Root Key pop-up menu to the note the sample actually is.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler Pitch controls in Logic Pro for Mac

Getting it into the arrangement

No. 155GAME CHANGER

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Shuffle the slice MIDI to rearrange the break

The generated MIDI plays the slices in the original order. Now shuffle the notes and the break rearranges itself.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler Slice mode in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 156

Section 14 · Quick Sampler Tricks

Convert Quick Sampler to Sampler for full control

Replace Quick Sampler with Sampler on the instrument channel strip and your current content transfers automatically. Do it when you need to work with more than one audio file at a time. It is a one-way trip: Sampler can load Quick Sampler settings, but Quick Sampler cannot open a Sampler setting.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler overview in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 15 · 10 tricks

Mixer Tricks.

The Mixer is where a collection of good parts becomes a record. These are the organisational and workflow tricks — the ones that stop a 60‑track session from becoming unmanageable.

Getting around the mixer

No. 157Start here

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

X shows and hides the Mixer

Press X (View > Show Mixer) to show and hide the Mixer in the main window, so you can flip between arrangement and mixer with one key. If you want the Mixer in its own window instead, press Command-2 (Window > Open Mixer).

X

Source Apple — Key commands for Global Commands in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Overview of mixing in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 158Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

⌥-click a fader to reset it to 0 dB

Option-click a channel strip's Volume fader to snap it back to 0 dB. It's the fastest way to undo a level you've talked yourself into.

⌥ + click

Source Apple — Set channel strip volume in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 159

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

⌥-click Solo for exclusive solo

Option-clicking an unsoloed channel strip solos it and unsolos every other channel strip — one gesture to hear one thing. Option-clicking any active Solo button clears all solos at once. Mute has its own bulk gesture, using Command rather than Option: Command-click a Mute button and every Mute button currently in the same state flips with it, including the output and master strips.

⌥ + click

Source Apple — Mute and solo channel strips in Logic Pro for Mac

Routing and organisation

No. 160GAME CHANGER

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

Use VCA faders for level groups without changing routing

A VCA changes the volume of each channel assigned to it without routing their audio through an aux, so nothing gets re-patched. One consequence: with post-fader sends, what each member sends to an effect follows the VCA, so pulling the VCA down pulls its reverb and delay sends down too, keeping the dry/wet balance. Use Pre Fader sends for anything that must stay constant.

Source Apple — Use VCA groups in Logic Pro for Mac · macProVideo - VCA Groups and Faders in Logic Pro X: What, Why, and How?

No. 161

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

Use Summing Stacks for processing groups

Select tracks and hit ⇧⌘D, then choose Summing Stack in the dialog that appears. Everything routes to one aux you can compress and EQ as a unit.

⌘⇧D

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac track stacks overview · Apple — Create and edit Track Stacks in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 162

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

Create a send and Logic makes the aux for you

Click a channel's Send slot and choose a bus. Logic creates the aux channel strip automatically, with that bus already set as its input — unless the bus is already in use as an input on another channel strip.

Source Apple — Send signals to multiple destinations in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Overview of aux channel strips in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

No. 163

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

Set sends to pre‑fader for headphone mixes and effects that must stay constant

Every send has three signal-flow modes, set from the send's pop-up menu: Post Pan (after fader and pan), Post Fader (follows volume but not pan) and Pre Fader (affected by neither). Use a post mode for reverb, so the effect tracks the part. Use Pre Fader for a headphone cue mix, or any send that must stay put while you ride the fader.

Source Apple — Route audio via send effects in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Why Logic Pro Rules - Pre-Fader vs Post-Fader vs Post-Pan Explained

No. 164

Section 15 · Mixer Tricks

Colour your tracks and the mixer follows

Mixer channels take the track colour. A consistent colour scheme means you find the vocal bus without reading a single label.

Source Apple — Change track colors in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Channel strip controls in Logic Pro for Mac

Plugins in the mixer

Bypass with ⌥-click, browse with the slot arrows

⌥-click an insert slot to bypass the plugin without opening it. To browse plugins, click the arrows at the right edge of the slot.

⌥ + click

Source Apple — Add, remove, move and copy plug-ins in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 166

Drag plugins between insert slots and between channels

Reorder your chain by dragging a plug-in up or down, or drag it to another channel strip to move it there. Hold ⌥ and drag it to an unused slot to copy rather than move.
