Section 16 · 14 tricks

Logic's Built-in Plugins.

The stock plugins worth knowing properly, and the specific controls that make each one worth reaching for.

Dynamics

No. 167

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Compressor — use the side‑chain filter before reaching for a multiband

Turn on the side-chain filter, set it to HP and sweep the frequency up until the kick stops triggering most of the gain reduction. Click Listen to hear what the detector hears. Switch Listen off again before you judge the mix.

Source Apple — Compressor side chain parameters in Logic Pro for Mac · Sound On Sound — Logic: Compression Sessions · MusicTech — Advanced Use Of The Logic Compressor

No. 168

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Multipressor — use it to control one problem band only

Bypass every band except the one you need. It becomes a dynamic EQ rather than a mix‑flattening machine.

Source Apple — Multipressor in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Multipressor frequency band controls in Logic Pro for Mac (MY)

No. 169

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Noise Gate — use the side chain to key one sound from another

Gate a white noise layer from the snare's signal and you have an instant layered snare that follows the performance.

Source Apple — Use Noise Gate in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 170

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Enveloper — reshape a transient without a compressor

The two Gain sliders either side of the display boost or cut the attack and release phases of any sound. Push Attack up to add snap to a soft kick. Pull it down and percussive sounds fade in more softly.

Source Apple — Enveloper in Logic Pro for Mac

EQ and tone

No. 171

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Channel EQ — turn on Analyzer and set it to Post

Seeing what you are cutting is worth more than any preset. Post‑EQ analysis shows the result rather than the source.

Source Apple — Channel EQ parameters in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 172GAME CHANGER

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Match EQ — steal a tone rather than guess at it

Learn a reference, learn your track, and Match EQ builds a filter curve from the difference. The Apply slider sets how hard that curve hits: under 100% reduces it, over 100% exaggerates it, and negative values invert its peaks and troughs. Raise Smoothing to even out a spiky curve.

Source Apple — Match EQ parameters in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Match EQ parameters in Logic Pro for Mac (MY) · Apple — Use Match EQ in Logic Pro for Mac

Time and space

No. 173GAME CHANGER

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

ChromaVerb — use the Damping display as the main control

The Damping EQ overlaid on the main display sets how much of each frequency stays in the reverb decay. Drag the high shelving dot down to shorten the high-end decay and the tail gets darker.

Source Apple — ChromaVerb display and Damping EQ in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 174

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Delay Designer — build rhythmic patterns, not echoes

Each tap has its own delay time plus independent filter cutoff and resonance, transpose, pan and level. Treat it as a sequencer for delay taps and build patterns rather than plain echoes.

Source Apple — Delay Designer Tap parameter bar in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 175

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Stereo Delay — set different times per side

Turn off Stereo Link, then set 1/8 on the left and dotted 1/8 on the right, so each side repeats at its own time.

Source Apple — Stereo Delay in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 176

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Tape Delay — turn up Flutter for analogue character

Flutter Rate and Intensity simulate the speed irregularities of an analogue tape transport, and the LFO adds further delay modulation. The Low and High Cut filters sit in the feedback path, so each repeat gets thinner or darker than the last.

Source Apple — Tape Delay in Logic Pro for Mac

Character and utility

No. 177

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Phat FX — one plugin, an entire character chain

Six effects modules in one window — Band-pass, Distortion, Mod FX, Bass Enhancer, Compressor and Filter — plus an assignable X/Y pad, three modulation sources (Env Follower, LFO 1, LFO 2) and an Effect Order strip. Distortion types include Bitcrusher, Diode, Dirt, Downsampler, Grit, Scream, Soft Saturation and Vari Drive.

Source Apple — Phat FX overview in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Phat FX processors in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 178

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Remix FX — perform DJ effects live

Real-time effects including Gater, Downsampler, Reverse and Tape Stop, played from buttons, sliders and XY pads. Apple built it for real-time effects common to electronic and dance music.

Source Apple — Remix FX in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 179GAME CHANGER

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Gain — use it to check phase, not just level

The Gain plugin's Phase Invert button gives you a quick phase check. Flip it, listen for the low end, keep whichever is bigger.

Source Apple — Gain controls in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 180

Section 16 · Logic's Built-in Plugins

Test Oscillator — reference tones for calibration

Generates sine and square waves at an adjustable frequency (1 kHz by default), plus white and pink noise, for use as reference tones.

Source Apple — Test Oscillator in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 17 · 14 tricks

More Tricks.

The ones that did not fit anywhere else: templates, key commands, project hygiene, bouncing and the small habits that quietly save hours.

Key commands and customisation

No. 181Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 17 · More Tricks

Open Key Commands with ⌥K and use the search box

Open Key Commands with ⌥K, type a term in the search field to find a command by name, then assign a key to it.

⌥K

Source Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 182

Section 17 · More Tricks

Save your key commands as a set and back it up

In the Key Commands window (⌥K), click the Actions button, choose Save As, name the set and click Save. That captures your whole set of custom shortcuts, including any Touch Bar assignments. Keep a copy of the file somewhere safe; losing a year of custom shortcuts to a reinstall is entirely avoidable.

Source Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 183

Section 17 · More Tricks

Save your go-to plug-in chains as channel strip settings

Set up a channel strip with the plug-ins you reach for most, then click the Setting button at the top of the channel strip and choose Save Channel Strip Setting as. A channel strip setting stores the plug-ins and their settings, so choosing it later from the same Setting pop-up menu brings back the whole chain at once.

Source Apple — Work with channel strip settings in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 184

Section 17 · More Tricks

Put your key commands on the Touch Bar or a controller button

In the Key Commands window, select a command, click Learn by Touch Bar, tap a Touch Bar button and give it a name. It then appears on the Touch Bar's Keyboard Shortcuts screen. For hardware, select the command (use the Search field) and press a button on your control surface. Its name appears in the Assignments field.

Source Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Assign controller buttons to key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

Templates and project management

No. 185GAME CHANGER

Section 17 · More Tricks

Build separate templates for writing, mixing and mastering

A writing template loads instantly with a handful of instruments. A mixing template has your buses and reference chain. They are different jobs and they deserve different starting points.

No. 186

Section 17 · More Tricks

Use Project Alternatives instead of Save As

File > Project Alternatives > New Alternative keeps every version inside one project. Apple's guide says alternatives are "saved as part of the project and share the same assets", so you are not duplicating gigabytes of recordings to try a different arrangement.

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 187

Section 17 · More Tricks

Keep a reference track in every project, muted at the top

A commercial track at the top of the session, routed to the master, muted. Unmute it whenever you lose perspective — which will be every hour.

No. 188

Section 17 · More Tricks

Name your bounce files with the date

“Mix_v3.wav” tells you nothing in six weeks. “Song_2026‑04‑18_mix3.wav” tells you everything.

Bouncing and export

No. 189Start here

Section 17 · More Tricks

⌘B bounces the project or the current section

Choose File > Bounce > Project or Section, or press ⌘B. With Cycle mode off and no regions selected, Logic bounces the whole project. With Cycle on, the bounce range matches the locators; with regions selected, it matches the selection. You can also set it with the Start and End value sliders. Select more than one destination file type to bounce several formats in one pass.

⌘B

Source Apple — Set the bounce range in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac · Why Logic Pro Rules — 10 Logic Pro X Key Commands That Will Rock Your Workflow

No. 190

Section 17 · More Tricks

Check the Normalize setting before you bounce

Both the project bounce and Bounce Regions in Place have a Normalize setting. Off leaves the level alone. Overload Protection Only turns the level down only where it would clip above 0 dB. On raises the level so the highest peak reaches the maximum possible without clipping.

Source Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 191

Section 17 · More Tricks

Bounce offline unless external MIDI or inputs are involved

Offline bouncing is typically faster than realtime. But only internal sources — audio and software instrument tracks — can bounce offline, not MIDI tracks or audio channel inputs. External MIDI sound sources routed to the Mixer through aux channels need Realtime. If you're unsure, choose Automatic and Logic decides, based on whether channels have plug-ins that need a realtime bounce.

Source Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 192

Section 17 · More Tricks

Leave room for tails at the end of the bounce range

To leave room for reverb and delay tails, push the End position past the last note with the End value slider in the Bounce dialog before you bounce. With Cycle mode on, you can drag the right locator instead, because the bounce range matches the locators. Then listen to the end of the file before you send it.

Source Apple — Set the bounce range in Logic Pro for Mac

Habits worth building

No. 193

Section 17 · More Tricks

Colour and name everything before you leave the session

Five minutes at the end of a session saves twenty at the start of the next one.

No. 194

Section 17 · More Tricks

Save a version before every major change

New Alternative, then experiment freely. Fear of breaking something is the biggest brake on creative decisions.

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac

Section 18 · 32 tricks

Logic Pro 11 Update.

Logic Pro 11 arrived in May 2024 with Session Players, the Chord track, Stem Splitter and ChromaGlow; Flashback Capture followed in 11.2. Stem Splitter and ChromaGlow need a Mac with Apple silicon, running Logic natively rather than in Rosetta. This section covers the new tools.

Source Apple Newsroom — Logic Pro takes music-making to the next level with new AI features (May 2024) · Apple — If you can't find ChromaGlow, Stem Splitter, or other Logic Pro features on Mac · Sound On Sound — Apple Logic Pro 11.2 review

Session Players — the fundamentals

No. 195

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use Follow Rhythm Of to lock players together

In the Session Player Editor, click Patterns and look under Follow Rhythm Of. Following the chord rhythm is on by default. For the Bass Player or Keyboard Player, choose a track from the Track pop-up menu to follow its rhythm. For the Drummer, click Patterns for the Kick and Snare kit pieces, then choose a track the same way.

Source Apple — Follow rhythm of chords and other tracks in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple (UK) — Follow rhythm of chords and other tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 196

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Session Player performances are per region, so write in sections

The Session Player Editor edits the performance of the selected region, and its Complexity and Intensity sliders adjust that region's performance. Give each song section its own region and set the sliders per region. That is how you get a verse that builds into a chorus.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface · Apple — The Session Player Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 197

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Change style without losing your settings

Before you audition styles, choose Keep Settings when Changing Style from the Preset pop-up menu in the Session Player Editor. Your performance settings then survive the switch, so you hear every style against the same settings. To protect just one parameter, click the lock next to the Fill Amount or Swing knob.

Source Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for iPad

No. 198

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Nudge Complexity or Intensity before you rebuild a part

The Complexity and Intensity sliders change the region's performance: higher means a busier or louder part. If a bar is not landing, try nudging those sliders before you rebuild the part from scratch.

Source Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface

No. 199

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Layer two Session Players on the same part

Put two Session Players on the same part: one playing simply, one playing busily, with the busy one low in the mix.

Bass Player

No. 200Start here

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Adjust the Complexity slider before you adjust anything else

Reach for the Complexity slider first: drag it higher for a more complex performance, lower for a plainer one. Low complexity in a verse and high in a chorus is an arrangement decision made with one slider.

Source Apple — Edit a Session Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface · Sound On Sound — Logic Pro: Session Players

No. 201

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Shape the bass articulations in Details

Click Details in the Session Player Editor for bass-specific controls: a Dead Notes knob for percussive, unpitched notes; a Slides knob for how often the player slides between and before notes; a Dynamic Mute button; and a Pickup Hits button for open-palm hits on beats 2 and 4. There are also probability controls for Buzz Trills and Double Stops.

Source Apple — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple (UK) — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 202

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Pair Bass Player with Studio Bass for its slides

The electric and acoustic Bass Players use dedicated MIDI events and articulations to create slides in the Studio Bass plug-in.

Source Apple — Edit a Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Session Players overview in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 203

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Set the Bass Player to follow a specific track's rhythm

In the Session Player Editor, click Patterns, then choose your guitar or piano track from the Track pop-up menu under Follow Rhythm Of. The bass then follows that part's rhythm.

Source Apple — Follow rhythm of chords and other tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

Keyboard Player

No. 204

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use the left- and right-hand controls independently

The left hand has its own Voicing and Style menus; the right hand has its own Voicing and Movement menus. Set the left hand's Style to Sustain Only or Simple and it stays out of the way while the right hand carries the chords, which is useful for comping behind a vocal.

Source Apple — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple (MD) — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 205

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Thin out the left hand without touching the right

Complexity and Intensity are different controls: Complexity sets how complex the part is, Intensity how loud and intense. Set them with the sliders, then use the left hand's Style menu (Sustain Only, Simple, Moderate, Complex) to make the left hand sparser or busier independently of the right hand.

Source Apple (MD) — Edit a Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac Session Player Editor interface

No. 206

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Convert to MIDI, then thin out the part

Control-click the Session Player region and choose Convert > Convert to MIDI Region. The result behaves like any other MIDI region, so open it in the Piano Roll and delete the left-hand notes to leave a lighter pad or comp.

Source Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 207

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use Keyboard Player as a writing tool, not a final part

Generate a progression, convert it to MIDI, then play the good bits yourself. The generated part becomes your reference.

Source Apple — Convert Session Player regions into MIDI or pattern regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 208

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Try the Synth Player styles, not just piano

Session Players include Synth Player styles. For keys: Rhythmic Chords, Modulated Pad and Simple Pad. For bass: 808 Bass, Pump Bass and Sequenced Bass. Choosing one loads a patch that uses Alchemy.

Source Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit a Synth Keyboard Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

The Chord track

No. 209Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Show the Chord track in Global Tracks

Press G to show the global tracks, then choose Track > Global Tracks > Configure Global Tracks and select Chord. Session Player regions without their own region chords follow the progression you enter there.

G

Source Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose which chords a Session Player region follows in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 210

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Generate chords from an existing region

Drag a MIDI or audio region onto the Chord track and Logic analyses it and adds its chords as a chord group. Or Control-click the region, choose Chords > Analyze Chords, then Chords > Apply Region Chords to Chord Track.

Source Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 211

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Resize chords by dragging their lower edges

Move the pointer over the lower-left or lower-right edge of a chord until it becomes the Resize pointer, then drag to shorten or lengthen it.

Source Apple — Move and resize chords in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 212

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use Pitch Source to keep parts off the Chord track

Select the region and open the Pitch Source pop-up in the Region inspector. Chord Track makes it follow your progression; Region Chords, Key Signature or Off take it off the Chord track. Use that for loops and parts you have already committed.

Source Apple — Control transposition with the Pitch Source parameter in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose which chords a Session Player region follows in Logic Pro for Mac

Stem Splitter

No. 213Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Split any mixed audio into stems

Control-click an audio region and choose Processing > Stem Splitter. Since 11.2 it separates up to six stems — vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and other — and it needs an Apple silicon Mac.

Source Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac · Why Logic Pro Rules — Logic Pro 11.2 Update is Out! Improved Stem Splitter · Production Expert — Apple Updates Logic Pro with Improved Stem Separation

No. 214

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use it on your own rough mixes, not just other people's records

It is especially handy for recovering a part from a bounce of your own song when the original session is gone.

Source Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 215

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Solo each stem and listen before you commit

Stem Splitter can leave artefacts: bits of a vocal sometimes land in the wrong stem, and results depend on how busy the mix is and how much reverb and delay it has. Solo each stem from its subtrack header and listen for artefacts before you build on it.

Source Sound On Sound — Logic Pro: How To Get The Best From The Stem Splitter · Sound On Sound — Logic Pro: How To Use The Stem Splitter · Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 216

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Try single stems as layers first

Tuck a split stem under your other parts before you rely on it on its own, and listen for artefacts either way.

No. 217Start here

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Make an instrumental with one preset

Stem Splitter's presets cover the common jobs in one click: Acapella gives you the vocal, Instrumental removes it. Or tick stems yourself. Selected stems come out individually, and two or more unselected stems are combined into a submix, which you extract by selecting the Submix checkbox.

Source Apple Newsroom — Logic Pro amplifies beat making on Mac and iPad with advanced new capabilities · Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 218

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Splitting adds rather than replaces

Clicking Apply creates a summing stack below the track holding the selected region, with the extracted stems on its subtracks. The original region is muted so you hear the stems straight away. It is still there if you want to go back to it.

Source Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac

ChromaGlow

No. 219GAME CHANGER

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

ChromaGlow is five saturation models in one plugin

The Model menu offers Retro Tube, Modern Tube, Magnetic, Squeeze and Analog Preamp, and each has its own character. Audition all five on the source before you start adjusting the other controls. ChromaGlow needs a Mac with Apple silicon, running Logic natively rather than in Rosetta.

Source Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac · MusicRadar — Apple Logic Pro for Mac 11/Logic Pro for iPad 2 review · Logic Studio Training — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro: 5 Models, 10 Styles Explained · Apple — If you can't find ChromaGlow, Stem Splitter, or other Logic Pro features on Mac

No. 220

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use Drive and Level Out together to stay level‑matched

Drive sets how much saturation you get, and Level Out sets the plug-in's output gain. When you push Drive, pull Level Out down so you are comparing at matched loudness. Otherwise you are only hearing louder, not better.

Source Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 221

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Try it before the compressor on the drum bus

Put ChromaGlow before the compressor on the drum bus, then swap the order and compare. Keep whichever sounds more controlled to you.

No. 222

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Use Bypass Below to keep the low end clean

ChromaGlow's Bypass Below control leaves everything under the frequency you set unsaturated, so the bass stays solid while the mids and top take the colour.

Source Apple — ChromaGlow in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 223

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Try it on the master at very low drive

Try a very small amount across the whole mix. If you can obviously hear it, back it off.

Flashback Capture and workflow additions

No. 224Start hereGAME CHANGER

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Flashback Capture retrieves what you just played

Logic's MIDI-only Capture Recording was renamed Flashback Capture in 11.2 and can now capture audio as well. A vocal run you played while Logic wasn't recording is recoverable too, as long as the project was playing. Use the control bar button, or press ⇧R.

⇧R

Source Sound On Sound — Apple Logic Pro 11.2 review · Apple — Capture a recent audio performance in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 225

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

MIDI capture works with the transport stopped

MIDI is caught whether the project is playing or stopped, so noodling with the song stopped is safe. Audio, added in 11.2, can be captured only while the project is playing, so leave the transport rolling when the mic is what you might want back.

Source Apple — Capture your most recent MIDI performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Capture a recent audio performance in Logic Pro for Mac · Sound On Sound — Apple Logic Pro 11.2 review

No. 226

Section 18 · Logic Pro 11 Update

Check plug-in compatibility after updating

Logic scans your plug-ins the first time it opens after an update. Before relying on a new version for real work, open the Plug-in Manager and look for 'failed validation' in the Compatibility column. Select that plug-in and click Reset & Rescan Selection. If it fails again, check with the developer for an update.

Source Apple — If Logic Pro for Mac hangs after updating · Apple — Use the Plug-in Manager in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — If you can't find a recently installed plug-in for Logic Pro for Mac or MainStage

Section 19 · 23 tricks

Logic Pro 12 Update.

Logic Pro 12 arrived on 28 January 2026. It runs only on Macs with Apple silicon and needs macOS Sequoia 15.6 or later. The headline additions are the Synth Player and Chord ID. This section covers what is new, plus an upgrade playbook for any major release.

Source Apple Newsroom — Introducing Apple Creator Studio (January 2026) · Production Expert — Logic Pro 12: AI features, new tools and Intel Mac support dropped

One requirement before anything else

Logic Pro 12 requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 15.6 or later. There is no Intel version. If you are still on an Intel machine, Logic Pro 11 is the end of the road — plan around that before you update anything.

Source Production Expert — Logic Pro 12: AI features, new tools and Intel Mac support dropped · Apple Newsroom — Introducing Apple Creator Studio (January 2026)

What's new in Logic Pro 12

No. 227GAME CHANGER

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Synth Player lives inside Bass Player and Keyboard Player

Synth Player is not a new Session Player. It is a set of styles inside the Bass Player and Keyboard Player you already have. Create a Bass Player or Keyboard Player track, open the Session Player Editor and choose a Synth style. Both players can follow the Chord track, so one progression drives bass and keys together.

Source Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Chords and Session Players in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 228

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Pick the Synth Keyboard style before you touch anything else

The Synth Keyboard Player has three styles: Rhythmic Chords, Modulated Pad and Simple Pad. Audition all three against the same chords before you start editing.

Source Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 229

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Synth Bass ships with three distinct characters

The Synth Bass Player has three styles: 808 Bass, Pump Bass and Sequenced Bass. Audition all three before you start editing the pattern.

Source Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

No. 230

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Shape the Pump Bass pump directly

Pump Bass gets its pumping from modulated ducking, like a sidechained compressor, and you can shape it. In the Session Player Editor, click the Details button. Drag the Amount knob vertically to set how hard it ducks, and the Shape knob to change the ducking curve.

Source Apple — Edit a Synth Bass Player performance in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 231

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Point Synth Player at a third-party synth

The performance and the sound source are separate. A Synth Player style loads an Alchemy patch by default, but you can use Synth Players with any software instrument plug-in or an external MIDI tone generator. You keep the chord-following performance and choose your own sound.

Source Apple — Intro to Synth Player styles in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 232GAME CHANGER

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Chord ID reads chords off audio, not just MIDI

Drag a guitar demo, a piano take or a rough bounce onto the Chord track. Chord ID analyses the region and adds the chords it finds to the Chord track as a chord group. It works on audio and MIDI regions, and Apple says it handles single instruments and full mixes.

Source Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

No. 233

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Check Chord ID's chords before you build on them

Chord ID writes what it finds straight onto the Chord track as a chord group. Play it back against the source before you build on it. If a chord is wrong, edit it on the Chord track: you can change the root note and chord type, add or remove extensions, and set a bass note other than the root.

Source Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Edit chords in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 234GAME CHANGER

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Everything downstream follows the Chord track

Once Chord ID has populated the Chord track, other tracks can lock to it. Apple: "By following the Chord track, multiple tracks — such as tracks using Step Sequencer, Session Player tracks, and other software instrument tracks — can play in sync harmonically." Set a Session Player region to follow with Control-click > Chords > Follow Global Chord Track; set a Step Sequencer pattern to follow by choosing Chord Track, which renames the note rows to chord degrees. One analysis pass can arrange several parts at once.

Source Apple — Choose which chords a Session Player region follows in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Chords and pitch in Step Sequencer in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Overview of chords in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 235

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Run Chord ID on your own old bounces

Lost the project but kept the bounce? Drag the bounce onto the Chord track and Chord ID adds its chords there as a chord group. Check them against the bounce, fix any that are wrong, then rebuild from there.

Source Apple — Analyze the chords in audio or MIDI regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

No. 236

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Preview sound packs before you download them

Open Logic Pro > Sound Library and click a sound pack to preview it before you commit to downloading. It is also where you reclaim space: click Manage Packs, then click Delete next to a pack you no longer need. The total space all installed packs use is shown at the top of the list, and each pack's size appears in the list.

Source Apple — Download additional sound packs in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes

No. 237

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Missing sounds after upgrading? Install the Legacy packs

Logic Pro 12.2 added three sound packs to reinstall content that was missing from the first release of Logic Pro 12: Logic Pro Legacy Patches, Logic Pro Legacy Instruments and Logic Pro Legacy Loops. Open Logic Pro > Sound Library and click Get next to the ones you need.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac release notes · Apple — Download additional sound packs in Logic Pro for Mac

No. 238

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Reanalyze and try each Character

When the mix changes, click Reanalyze in Mastering Assistant so it analyses the project again. Then try the Character options: Transparent (the default), Clean, Valve and Punch. A/B each against the master you signed off on before you call it finished. Transparent, Punch and Valve require an Apple silicon Mac.

Source Apple — Mastering Assistant parameters in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Use Mastering Assistant in Logic Pro

Before you update

No. 239GAME CHANGER

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Logic Pro 12 drops Intel Macs entirely

Logic Pro 12 requires a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15.6 or later. If you are on an Intel Mac you can't run it, so check your machine before you plan an upgrade.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac - Technical Specifications · Apple Support — Logic Pro - Tech Specs

No. 240GAME CHANGER

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Never update in the middle of a paid project

The one rule that matters. Finish and deliver, then update. A new version halfway through a mix is a self‑inflicted deadline problem.

No. 241

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Back up the current version before you update

Use Apple's procedure. Make a folder in Applications named for the version (for example "Logic Pro 11.1.2"), select Logic Pro and choose File > Compress "Logic Pro", then move Logic Pro.zip into that folder. If the update causes problems, reinstall the backed-up version.

Source Apple Support — Back up Logic Pro for Mac

No. 242

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Back up your key commands and channel strip settings

Choose Logic Pro > Key Commands > Edit, click the Actions button, choose Save As, name your set and save it somewhere safe, such as an external drive. Your channel strip settings live in ~/Music/Audio Music Apps/Channel Strip Settings, so copy that folder too.

Source Apple Support — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac · Logic Studio Training Wiki — Channel strip settings · macProVideo — Demystifying Logic Pro X's Plug-In Settings, Channel Strip Settings & Patches

No. 243

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Consolidate and archive your three most important projects

File > Project Management > Consolidate on each, then copy them to a separate drive. If the new version changes something, you have untouched originals.

Source Apple Support — Consolidate assets in a Logic Pro for Mac project

No. 244

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Check your critical third‑party plugins against the new version first

Check each plug-in developer's compatibility notes before you update Logic, not after.

No. 245

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Note your current I/O and buffer settings

Screenshot your Audio settings before you update — output device, input device and I/O buffer size. It takes five seconds, and if anything about your setup looks different afterwards you can restore the exact configuration you were working with instead of guessing at it.

Source Apple Support — Avoid system overloads in Logic Pro for Mac · macProVideo — Logic Pro X Audio Preferences Explained

No. 246

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Update macOS and Logic separately, a week apart

If something breaks, you want to know which of the two did it.

After you update

No. 247

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Read the new Key Commands list for additions

After every update, choose Logic Pro > Key Commands > Edit and browse for commands you haven't seen before. Click Unused to show commands that have no shortcut yet. For any you'll use, select it, click Learn by Key Label and press the keys you want.

Source Apple Support — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac

No. 248

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Test your bounce path end to end before you need it

Bounce a short section to every format you deliver in, so any problem turns up before a deadline does.

No. 249

Section 19 · Logic Pro 12 Update

Give yourself a deliberate hour to explore

Not on a project. Open a scratch session and use every new feature once. An hour of play beats a month of accidental discovery.

Plain-English definitions

Glossary

Every Logic word used in this book, in plain English. Each definition cites where it was checked.

Audio
Recorded sound — a voice, a guitar, anything captured through a microphone or input — stored in audio files and placed on audio tracks as audio regions.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Automation
Recorded or drawn changes to a control over time — a fader rising, a filter opening — that Logic plays back for you. Volume, pan, sends and most plug-in settings can be automated.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Overview of automation in Logic Pro for Mac

Auxalso: aux channel strip, auxiliary
An aux (auxiliary) channel strip receives sound sent to it over a bus, so it can be processed or combined into a submix.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Backupalso: backups, Project Alternative
Each time you save, Logic keeps a backup of the project — up to ten per project alternative — which you can go back to with File > Revert to.

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups in Logic Pro for Mac

Bouncealso: bouncing, export
Turning your project, or part of it, into a new audio file. Bounce in Place does this to selected regions, keeping their plug-ins and automation in the result.

Source Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview

Bufferalso: I/O buffer, buffer size
The chunk of audio your Mac processes at a time. A smaller I/O buffer means less latency but more strain on the processor; too small for your Mac and you hear clicks, pops and crackles.

Source Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

Busalso: buses, busses
A route that carries sound from a send to an aux channel strip, where it can be processed or mixed with other tracks.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Channel stripalso: channel strips
The on-screen version of a strip on a mixing desk: a volume fader, a pan knob, a Mute button, and slots for inputs, outputs, sends and effects. Your tracks' sound runs through their channel strips.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Channel strip controls in Logic Pro for Mac

Chord track
A global track that holds your song's chord progression, so Session Players can follow the same chords and play in sync.

Source Apple — Chords and Session Players in Logic Pro for Mac

Compalso: comping, comps
Short for composite: the best sections of several takes combined into one performance, shown in the top lane of a take folder.

Source Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

Count-inalso: count in
A lead-in of bars or beats before recording starts, so you are ready to come in.

Source Apple — Recording project settings in Logic Pro for Mac

Cyclealso: cycle area, cycle mode
A section of the timeline that plays over and over while Cycle mode is on — for writing, practising a part or recording several takes.

Source Apple — Use the cycle area in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Drum Machine Designeralso: DMD
A drum instrument laid out as pads. Every pad you fill gets its own subtrack and channel strip, so each drum sound can be processed on its own.

Source Apple — Drum Machine Designer in Logic Pro for Mac

Fadealso: fades, fade-in, fade-out
A gradual change in volume at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out) of a region. A short fade-in also prevents the click you can get when audio starts abruptly.

Source Why Logic Pro Rules — How to Get the Most Out of Logic Pro X's Fade Tool · Apple — Snap to zero in the Logic Pro for Mac Audio Track Editor

Flexalso: Flex Time, flex markers
Flex Time changes the timing inside recorded audio by stretching and squeezing the audio between markers, instead of cutting it into pieces.

Source Apple — Flex tool time stretching in Logic Pro for Mac

Gain
A region's level. The Region inspector's Gain setting changes how loud an audio region plays without changing the file.

Source Apple — Change the gain of audio regions in the Tracks area in Logic Pro for Mac

Global tracksalso: global track
Song-wide tracks above your regular tracks — by default Arrangement, Marker, Signature and Tempo. Press G to show them.

Source Apple — Show and hide global tracks in Logic Pro for Mac

Inspectoralso: Region inspector
A panel that shows settings for whatever is selected. The Region inspector, for example, shows the playback settings of the selected regions.

Source Apple — Use the Region inspector in Logic Pro for Mac

Key commandalso: key commands, shortcut, keyboard shortcut
A keyboard shortcut for a Logic command. You can find, search and change them in the Key Commands window (Option-K).

Source Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac

Latency
A delay between a sound going in and you hearing it come out. Processing takes time, so plug-ins and the audio buffer both add latency — which you notice most while recording.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Work with plug-in latencies in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Configure audio devices to use with Logic Pro for Mac

Library
The panel where you choose a patch for the selected track: categories on the left, patches on the right. Click the Library button in the control bar to open it.

Source Apple — Choose patches in the Library in Logic Pro for Mac

Locatorsalso: left locator, right locator
The left and right locators mark the start and end of the cycle area.

Source Apple — Use the cycle area in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Markeralso: markers
A named flag on the timeline for labelling parts of your song and jumping between them.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac markers overview

Marquee toolalso: marquee
A tool that selects a range of time instead of whole regions. Drag across one or more tracks and only the part inside is selected, ready to move, cut, copy or delete.

Source Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac

Metronome
A regular click that marks the beat so you can play in time.

Source Apple — Metronome project settings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

MIDI
Musical Instrument Digital Interface. MIDI is note information — which pitch, how long, how loud — sent between keyboards, computers and instruments. It is not sound itself; an instrument turns it into sound.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Use MIDI plug-ins in Logic Pro for Mac

Mixer
The window that shows every track's channel strip side by side, so you can balance levels and set up effects. Press X to show or hide it.

Source Apple — Overview of mixing in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Patchalso: patches
A ready-made sound you load onto a track. It can include the instrument, its effects and other channel strip settings.

Source Apple — Patches in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose patches in the Library in Logic Pro for Mac

Piano Rollalso: Piano Roll Editor
The editor that shows the notes in a MIDI region as bars on a grid beside a piano-style keyboard, where you add, move and edit them. Press P with a MIDI region selected.

Source Apple — Overview of the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

Playhead
The vertical line that shows where playback is. Drag it to hear a different point in the song.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Plug-inalso: plugin, plug-ins, plugins
An add-on that gives a track its sound or changes it — usually a software instrument or an effect.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Quantizealso: quantise, quantization
Moving notes so they start exactly on the nearest point of a timing grid, tightening up playing that is slightly early or late.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Quick Sampler
A built-in instrument that turns a single audio file into something you can play on a keyboard. To work with more than one audio file at once, use Sampler instead.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler overview in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Choose a Quick Sampler mode in Logic Pro for Mac

Regionalso: regions
A block on a track that holds a piece of your recording. Audio regions point to part of an audio file; MIDI regions hold notes. You build a song by moving, copying and editing regions.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Capture your most recent MIDI performance in Logic Pro for Mac

Sendalso: sends
A control on a channel strip that routes its sound along a bus to an aux channel strip. Choose a bus in a Send slot and Logic creates the aux for you.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Send signals to multiple destinations in Logic Pro for Mac

Session Playeralso: Session Players, Drummer, Bass Player, Keyboard Player, Synth Player
Logic's built-in virtual musicians. Drummer was joined by Bass Player and Keyboard Player in Logic Pro 11, and by Synth Player in Logic Pro 12. Bass Player and Keyboard Player can follow your chord progression.

Source Apple Newsroom — Logic Pro takes music-making to the next level with new AI features (May 2024) · Apple Newsroom — Introducing Apple Creator Studio (January 2026) · Apple — Chords and Session Players in Logic Pro for Mac

Smart Controls
A set of on-screen knobs for shaping the selected track's sound — usually tone and EQ, reverb and other effects — without opening each plug-in. Press B to show them.

Source Apple — Overview of Smart Controls in Logic Pro for Mac

Snap
Makes edits land on the nearest grid position — a bar, a beat or a finer division — so things stay in time. Turn it on or off with the button next to the Snap menu.

Source Apple — Snap items to the grid in Logic Pro for Mac

Software instrumentalso: instrument, software instruments
An instrument that runs inside Logic — a synthesizer, a sampler or a re-creation of a vintage instrument — played with MIDI from a keyboard or from MIDI regions.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Instruments introduction for Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Use MIDI plug-ins in Logic Pro for Mac

Stemalso: stems, Stem Splitter
One part of a mix on its own — vocals, drums, bass and so on. Stem Splitter pulls stems out of a single mixed recording, on Macs with Apple silicon.

Source Apple — Extract vocal and instrumental stems with Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — If you can't find ChromaGlow, Stem Splitter, or other Logic Pro features on Mac

Step Sequencer
An editor for building beats and patterns one step at a time on a grid of rows. Each row can have its own length and step rate.

Source Apple — Edit Step Sequencer pattern, row, and step settings in Logic Pro for Mac

Takealso: takes, take folder
Each pass you record over the same spot is a take. Logic keeps them in a take folder, and its pop-up menu lists them so you can pick one.

Source Apple — Preview take recordings in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

Tempoalso: bpm
The speed of the music in beats per minute (bpm). At 120 bpm there are 120 beats every minute.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Track
A horizontal lane in the Tracks area where you record, play back and edit regions. Each track plays through its own channel strip in the Mixer.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Track Stackalso: Track Stacks, folder stack, summing stack
A group of tracks under one main track. A folder stack just keeps them tidy; a summing stack also routes them to a bus so you can process them together.

Source Apple — Logic Pro for Mac track stacks overview

Tracks area
The main part of the Logic window, where your tracks and their regions sit.

Source Apple — Select parts of regions in Logic Pro for Mac · Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

Transientalso: transients
The sharp start of a sound, like a drum hit. Logic can detect transients — for example to cut a loop into slices in Quick Sampler.

Source Apple — Quick Sampler Slice mode in Logic Pro for Mac

Velocity
How hard a note was played, from 0 to 127. It usually sets the note's loudness, and can shape other parts of the sound too.

Source Apple — Logic Pro Glossary (Logic Pro 10.7 guide) · Apple — Edit velocity in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

The end

That’s the 249. Go finish the song.

Come back whenever you get stuck. The search bar is always at the top.

Step 1Start here

Start Here · Step 1

Learn the four parts of the screen

The control bar runs across the top: play, record, volume, and the display showing where you are in the song and its tempo. The big middle area is the Tracks area, where you record and arrange. The Library sits on the left and holds sounds. The Inspector shows settings for whatever you have selected.

Source Apple — Main window interface (10.7 guide) · Apple — Inspector interface

Step 2Start here

Start Here · Step 2

Know what a track and a region are

A track is one lane in the Tracks area: one instrument or one microphone. A region is a block of recorded audio or MIDI sitting on a track. You move, copy and cut regions to build a song.

Source Apple — Main window interface (10.7 guide) · Apple — Create tracks

Step 3Start here

Start Here · Step 3

Add a track

Click the Add Tracks button (the + above the track headers). In the New Tracks dialog pick Software Instrument to play sounds from a keyboard, Audio to record a microphone or guitar, or Drummer for a virtual drummer that plays a region for you.

Source Apple — Create tracks · Apple — Drummer overview (10.7 guide)

Step 4Start here

Start Here · Step 4

Pick a sound in the Library

Select the track, open the Library, choose a category on the left and a patch on the right. The track now plays that sound.

Y

Source Apple — Choose a patch

Step 5Start here

Start Here · Step 5

Play it without a keyboard

No MIDI keyboard? Turn on Musical Typing and play notes on your computer keys. Z and X move down and up an octave. A software instrument track must be selected.

⌘K

Source Apple — Play software instruments

Step 6Start here

Start Here · Step 6

Play, stop, and go back to the start

Space starts and stops playback. Return jumps the playhead back to the beginning of the project.

Space

Source Apple — Transport key commands (10.7 guide) · Apple — Control playback (10.7 guide)

Step 7Start here

Start Here · Step 7

Record

Select the track, press R, play, then press Space to stop. A new region appears on the track with what you played.

R

Source Apple — Record to multiple audio tracks

Step 8Start here

Start Here · Step 8

Undo anything

Made a mistake? Undo steps back one edit at a time; Redo puts it back. Experiment freely.

⌘Z

Source Apple — Undo and redo edits

Step 9Start here

Start Here · Step 9

Save often

Save writes the project to disk. Logic also keeps backups of earlier saves you can revert to from the File menu.

⌘S

Source Apple — Use project alternatives and backups

Step 10Start here

Start Here · Step 10

Export a file you can share

Bounce turns your project into an audio file, such as a WAV or MP3, that plays anywhere.

⌘B

Source Apple — Bounce a project to an audio file
